input: Take a paternity leave planning meeting with HR

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The expected birth or adoption date determines the urgency of scheduling the meeting and the timeline for the leave itself.
Knowing whether this meeting is just to get information or to also submit formal paperwork changes what needs to be prepared beforehand.
The length of leave the user intends to take affects what needs to be negotiated or approved with HR.
Whether the user has a specific HR contact or needs to find the right person first affects the very first action to take.
Whether the meeting is in-person, by phone, or virtual affects how to set it up and what documents to bring or share.
Whether the user wants to lead the agenda or let HR guide the meeting shapes what preparation is needed and which questions to prepare.
Knowing what the user needs to walk away with — confirmed dates, signed forms, a coverage plan — defines what a successful meeting looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Plan and hold a paternity leave HR meeting
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to schedule and conduct a meeting with HR to plan their upcoming paternity leave.

questions.title: When is your baby's due or arrival date?
questions.description: Understanding the expected arrival date establishes the urgency of the meeting and the leave start date to discuss with HR.

questions.title: Is this meeting to gather info or submit formal paperwork?
questions.description: Clarifying the purpose of the meeting determines what documents and questions need to be prepared in advance.

questions.title: How long are you planning to take for paternity leave?
questions.description: The intended duration of leave shapes what needs to be discussed, approved, or negotiated during the meeting.

questions.title: Do you already know which HR contact to reach out to?
questions.description: Identifying whether the user has a named HR contact determines whether finding the right person is itself a first step.

questions.title: Will the meeting be in-person, by phone, or virtual?
questions.description: The format of the meeting affects how it is scheduled and what materials need to be prepared or shared ahead of time.

questions.title: Do you want to drive the agenda or let HR lead it?
questions.description: The user's preferred role in the meeting determines how much preparation is needed and whether a personal agenda or question list should be drafted.

questions.title: What must you walk away from this meeting having confirmed?
questions.description: Defining the concrete outputs — approved dates, signed leave forms, a handover plan — sets the success criteria for the meeting.
